content.text:
I read all six project documents and found no conflicts and no reason to rule out any candidate.

- **Rate budget:** `rate_allocation.md` gives 8 kHz, which matches the value recorded in the earlier step. Nothing else mentions a rate.
- **Threshold range:** only the task brief states the 20–60 GeV range, so nothing contradicts it.
- **Deployability:** `candidate_specs.md` says all three algorithms fit the FPGA resource budget (LUTs and DSPs). `links.md` says the 25 Gb/s links have enough bandwidth for all of them.
- **Emulation caveats:** none of the documents lists any. `simulation_summary_2025.md` reports the same efficiencies as the earlier step: L2 92%, L3 85% and L1 74%, all at 35 GeV.
- **Other documents:** `meeting_notes_2026-06-03.md` and `schedule.md` are not relevant to the choice. They cover the September menu review and a Q4 firmware freeze.

There are gaps to keep in mind, even though they are not conflicts:

- **Latency and timing:** no document covers latency or timing for any candidate. L2 and L3 are the more complex algorithms, so this is the main open deployability risk.
- **Single threshold:** the 2025 efficiencies exist only at 35 GeV. Later steps should run the simulation across the threshold range, not rely on that one point.
- **Thin documentation:** the documents are short and unversioned, so the lack of caveats may just mean none were written down.

I recorded zero conflicts, zero candidates ruled out and zero emulation caveats.

content.text: Nothing rules out any candidate, so I'll scan all three.

I ran the coarse threshold scan for all three candidates and recorded the efficiencies. All three passed the deployability check. `candidate_specs.md` says each fits the FPGA resource budget, and no other document rules one out. Signal efficiency at the 8 kHz allocated rate (%), 100,000 events per point:

| Threshold (GeV) | Algorithm-L1 | Algorithm-L2 | Algorithm-L3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | 69.98 | 86.88 | 77.96 |
| 30 | 72.42 | 90.75 | 85.63 |
| 40 | 74.01 | 91.56 | 83.21 |
| 50 | 70.09 | 87.82 | 79.38 |
| 60 | 63.12 | 78.00 | 72.36 |

- **Best point:** Algorithm-L2 at 40 GeV gives the highest efficiency in the scan, at 91.56%.
- **Ranking:** Algorithm-L2 is highest at every threshold. Algorithm-L3 is second at every threshold, and Algorithm-L1 is lowest at every threshold.
- **Peak position:** Algorithm-L1 and Algorithm-L2 peak at 40 GeV. Algorithm-L3 peaks at 30 GeV.
- **Consistency with 2025:** The values at 30–40 GeV are close to the earlier 35 GeV emulation results of 92%, 85% and 74%.

The scan steps are 10 GeV, so the true peak for each algorithm could lie between points. A finer scan around 30–50 GeV for Algorithm-L2 would settle the threshold choice.
Best region is around 35-45 GeV for L2 (and L3 as the runner-up). I'll scan L2 and L3 more finely.

I ran the finer scan for L2 and L3 and recorded the results. L2 is still clearly ahead, but the L2 scan is noisy, so its best threshold isn't well pinned down.

| Algorithm | Threshold (GeV) | Efficiency (%) |
|---|---|---|
| L2 | 34 | 93.125 |
| L2 | 37 | 90.843 |
| L2 | 43 | 91.257 |
| L2 | 46 | 90.138 |
| L3 | 32 | 84.364 |
| L3 | 35 | 86.232 |
| L3 | 38 | 83.734 |

- **L2:** It is best at 34 GeV (93.1%), but the curve is not smooth. Efficiency drops to 90.8% at 37 GeV, then rises slightly to 91.6% at 40 GeV (from the earlier scan) and 91.3% at 43 GeV. That is a flat plateau of about 90–93% from roughly 34 to 46 GeV, with a spread of about 2.5%. I estimate the noise at about 1.5%, so the 34 GeV peak may be partly a fluctuation.
- **L3:** It peaks at 35 GeV (86.2%). That is about 5–7 points below L2 at comparable thresholds, so L3 is not competitive.
- **Edge check:** Both optima are well inside the 20–60 GeV range, so neither sits on the edge.

I didn't repeat any points to test the noise directly. The L2 recommendation holds anywhere in the 34–43 GeV plateau, and I would pick a threshold near the low end of it.

content.text:
**Recommendation: Algorithm-L2 (iterative topological clustering with a learned calibration) at a 34 GeV threshold.**

- **Efficiency:** the emulation gives 93.1% signal efficiency at the allocated 8 kHz. That is the highest of the three candidates.
- **Runner-up:** Algorithm-L3 (sliding-window clustering with a learned calibration) peaks at 86.2% at 35 GeV. L2 is about 7 points ahead.
- **Third place:** Algorithm-L1 (fixed-window sum) peaks at about 74% at 40 GeV.
- **Constraints:**
  - 34 GeV is inside the 20–60 GeV range, and the L2 optimum is not at the edge of the scan.
  - All three candidates are listed in `candidate_specs.md`, and the document says all fit the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs).
  - `links.md` says the optical links have enough bandwidth for all of them.
  - The documents show no conflicts on rate, threshold range or deployability, and no caveats on the emulation.
- **Threshold stability:** L2 stays between 90% and 93% from 30 to 46 GeV, a spread of about 2.5%. The emulation noise is about 1.5%, so 34 GeV is not clearly better than 30–43 GeV. Anywhere in that range gives roughly 91–93%.
- **Earlier 2025 result:** it gave L2 at 92% at 35 GeV, which agrees with the new scan.

**Caveats:**
- The documents say nothing about latency, which is the main deployability risk for an iterative algorithm. They only state that resources and link bandwidth are sufficient. It should be checked against the Level-1 latency budget before the firmware freeze in Q4.
- The efficiency numbers come from simulation only.
- If L2 turns out not to meet the latency budget, the fallback is L3 at 35 GeV.

I recorded the result with `record_results`. There is no separate submission tool, so this message is the submission.
